newsitem.title: ITALY: Magistrate says new Mafia turncoat is major source.
newsitem.headline: Magistrate says new Mafia turncoat is major source.

text.p: A leading magistrate said on Wednesday that former Sicilian Mafia boss Francesco Di Carlo had been talking to police for several months and that his information was of major significance.

"I consider Francesco di Carlo to be the new Buscetta," Palermo prosecuting magistrate Guido Lo Forte told reporters in Rome during a break in the trial of former Italian prime minister and life senator Giulio Andreotti.
"Francesco Di Carlo has been working with us for several months and his collaboration, for the depth and seriousness of his testimony, can be equated with that of Buscetta."
Former mobster Tommaso Buscetta, who became the first important Mafioso to cooperate with the law in 1984, is the star prosecution witness at Andreotti's trial for alleged Mafia links.
Buscetta, who lives mainly in the United States under a witness protection programme, has publicly linked Andreotti to Sicilians who prosecutors say have Mafia ties.

Di Carlo, 51, who British papers say was known in London underworld circles as "Frank the Strangler", was serving a 25 year sentence in a British prison for heroin trafficking but was transferred to Italy this year.
He has been linked by other turncoats to the death of Italian banker Roberto Calvi in London in 1982.
Calvi, dubbed "God's Banker" because his Banco Ambrosiano which handled Vatican investments, was found hanging under London's Blackfriar's Bridge. An open verdict was recorded in the case.
Lo Forte said Di Carlo, who was a boss in the San Giuseppe Jato area of Sicily, was giving an insight into the history of the Mafia over the last two decades.
"For us he is a reliable collaborator," he said, without providing any examples of Di Carlo's testimony.
